meta.name: Country Radar
meta.method: 10 fixed signal families; country-specific current development, impact and direction indicator.

items.development: Business services and manufacturing exports are recovering, while consumption and construction remain weak.
items.impact: Growth is concentrated in a few sectors, leaving the recovery fragile.

items.development: August inflation rose to 3.1%, driven by energy and fuel costs.
items.impact: Global energy shocks are again putting pressure on household budgets and monetary policy.

items.development: Goods exports are improving, while services exports remain below normal and companies see US tariffs and Chinese competition as risks.
items.impact: External demand is supportive, but changes in the trade regime increase the risk to the export model.

items.development: Corporate investment is shifting toward automation, AI, data centres, energy and defence infrastructure.
items.impact: Capital moving into new technology and infrastructure strengthens the economy's capacity to adapt.

items.development: Investment intentions have turned slightly positive from a low base, although borrowing costs remain restrictive.
items.impact: A restart in capital spending is positive, but a strong investment cycle has not yet formed.

items.development: The government eased long-term project appraisal rules to make infrastructure approvals easier.
items.impact: Making more infrastructure projects economically viable could expand capacity.

items.development: Planning and regulatory constraints are making delivery of major infrastructure and construction projects more difficult.
items.impact: Even where capital is available, slow execution could delay the transition.

items.development: Hiring difficulties have eased overall, but shortages persist in technical and specialist roles.
items.impact: A softer labour market provides short-term relief, while strategic skills gaps remain.

items.development: Average private rent rose 3.8% year on year in August to £1,400, with the London average reaching £2,332.
items.impact: Housing costs are putting pressure on incomes and reducing relocation appeal.

items.development: Work visas fell 18% over the past year and the Worker category fell 30%, with applications continuing to decline after policy changes.
items.impact: A smaller pool of international skilled workers could make long-term talent access more difficult.

items.development: International tourist spending rose 10.9% year on year in July to €18.2 billion.
items.impact: A strong services and tourism engine continues to support economic activity.

items.development: National inflation rose to 4.3% in August and EU-harmonised inflation to 4.6%.
items.impact: A renewed rise in energy and external price shocks could squeeze real incomes and consumption.

items.development: Foreign tourist spending rose 7.8% year on year in the first seven months, exceeding €82 billion.
items.impact: Strong international demand continues to support services exports and employment.

items.development: Spain increased planned investment in the electricity grid through 2030 by 30% to more than €17 billion.
items.impact: Scaling electrification and renewable-energy capacity strengthens energy resilience.

items.development: The government announced roughly €13 billion in airport investment and more than €1.2 billion in research investment.
items.impact: Large-scale transport and science investment supports future productivity capacity.

items.development: The 2027–2031 airport investment programme will create roughly €13 billion of new capacity.
items.impact: Expanding tourism and international connectivity infrastructure strengthens the current economic engine.

items.development: The EU partially approved Spain's sixth NextGenerationEU payment while assessment of some targets continues.
items.impact: Most funding is progressing, but remaining milestones still require close monitoring of execution capacity.

items.development: Spain's population reached 49.80 million on 1 July, rising by around 444,000 in one year.
items.impact: Migration-driven population growth broadens the labour base against ageing.

items.development: House prices rose 12.2% year on year in the second quarter, with existing homes up 12.9%.
items.impact: Housing costs rising faster than wages increase affordability and relocation costs in major cities.

items.development: A large migration wave in Ceuta strained accommodation capacity and brought migration policy back to the centre of the social and political agenda.
items.impact: Tensions around migration management could increase policy uncertainty for foreign workers.

items.development: GDP grew 2.3% in the second quarter, while industrial production fell 0.3% in July and services output rose 3%.
items.impact: Services support growth, but weakness in industry limits a more balanced expansion.

items.development: The CBRT is monitoring high and volatile global energy prices as a clear upside risk to inflation.
items.impact: Dependence on energy imports keeps inflation and the current account sensitive to external geopolitical shocks.

items.development: Exports rose 8.1% in August, while imports grew faster at 10.5%.
items.impact: Export growth is positive, but faster import growth limits gains in the external balance.

items.development: Industrial production fell 0.3% year on year in July and construction output fell 4.7%.
items.impact: Weak real output could slow new industrial capacity and transformation investment.

items.development: A liquidity squeeze in investment funds affected TRY 891 billion of assets and triggered a sharp stock-market sell-off.
items.impact: Financial-market volatility may raise the risk perception of both domestic and foreign capital.

items.development: Construction output fell 4.7% year on year in July, signalling weaker physical investment activity.
items.impact: A weak pace of infrastructure and construction investment may constrain the capital base for growth.

items.development: The CBRT and regulators raised repo funding to TRY 300 billion during the fund crisis, providing rapid market liquidity.
items.impact: The fast intervention appears to have reduced near-term systemic spillover risk.

items.development: Unemployment was 8.1%, while the number of paid employees rose 1.7% year on year in July.
items.impact: Employment continues to rise, but there is not yet a strong acceleration signal in the labour market.

items.development: August CPI was 31.51%, while annual inflation in housing and energy reached 39.77%.
items.impact: High living and housing costs weigh on real purchasing power and relocation economics.

items.development: September operations targeting LGBTQ+ groups and detentions of protesters drew criticism from European institutions and human-rights organisations.
items.impact: Uncertainty around rights and lifestyle may reduce relocation appeal for some international talent.

items.development: The Fed described economic activity as solid, consumption as resilient, and productivity and capital investment as strong.
items.impact: The economy's main growth engines continue to operate despite a high-interest-rate environment.

items.development: August CPI rose to 3.4%, while energy prices increased 2.1% month on month and gasoline 3.9%.
items.impact: Renewed energy-driven inflation raises the risk that interest rates stay higher for longer.

items.development: The United States and China are discussing extending their fragile trade truce ahead of the 24 September summit.
items.impact: Keeping tensions contained reduces trade and supply-chain uncertainty, although no durable solution has yet emerged.

items.development: Some battery and electric-vehicle investments were cancelled or delayed after EV incentives were rolled back.
items.impact: A slower automotive transition could weaken next-generation vehicle manufacturing capacity relative to China.

items.development: The Fed described capital investment as strong, while technology and data-centre spending remains elevated.
items.impact: Continued corporate investment appetite supports productivity and future growth capacity.

items.development: The 10-year Treasury yield is approaching 5%, with high public debt becoming one factor pushing up financing costs.
items.impact: More expensive long-term financing raises the cost of public and private infrastructure investment.

items.development: The Fed raised the policy rate by 25 basis points to 3.75–4% as inflation remained elevated.
items.impact: Policy response capacity remains strong, but higher rates create counter-pressure on growth.

items.development: The economy added 162,000 jobs in August and unemployment remained at 4.1%.
items.impact: The labour market remains resilient, although its growth pace is more limited than in earlier periods.

items.development: Mortgage rates rose to 6.76%, while homebuilder confidence fell to a 12-month low of 32.
items.impact: Financing costs are making housing affordability and household mobility materially harder.

items.development: The $100,000 fee on new H-1B applications was extended for another year and legal proceedings continue.
items.impact: Higher costs for hiring skilled foreign workers could push technology companies to shift talent strategies abroad.

items.development: The non-oil private-sector PMI rose from 52.7 to 55.3 in August.
items.impact: Faster non-oil activity supports the diversified growth model.

items.development: Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains far below normal levels because of the war.
items.impact: Exposure of the energy and logistics hub to a critical maritime chokepoint remains a major geopolitical risk.

items.development: Non-oil foreign trade grew 13.1% in the first half to AED 1.94 trillion.
items.impact: Broader trade partners and non-oil exports strengthen external-demand resilience.

items.development: Capital and public strategies are scaling AI, advanced technology, logistics and infrastructure as priority sectors.
items.impact: Shifting growth from hydrocarbons toward higher-value sectors supports structural diversification.

items.development: The UAE attracted AED 177.3 billion of FDI in 2025, recording a fourth consecutive record year.
items.impact: Strong foreign-capital inflows support the country's long-term role as an investment hub.

items.development: Dubai approved AED 3.5 billion for the first phase of a new 80 km transport corridor.
items.impact: Scaling transport capacity alongside population and economic growth reduces infrastructure bottlenecks.

items.development: A new rail-freight corridor linking Fujairah port with Abu Dhabi's industrial zone entered service.
items.impact: Operational alternative logistics routes strengthen system adaptability against Hormuz risk.

items.development: The government is increasingly aligning education, AI and private-sector careers through national talent programmes.
items.impact: Developing local skilled labour can reduce structural reliance on foreign labour over time.

items.development: Dubai real-estate transaction volumes fell 37% year on year in August and transaction value fell 44%.
items.impact: Market cooling may ease price pressure, but it does not yet prove meaningful relief in living costs.

items.development: Green, Golden and virtual-work visas continue to provide skilled and remote workers with long-term residence options without traditional sponsorship.
items.impact: Flexible long-term residence keeps relocation access strong for international talent.

items.development: Banque de France cut its 2026 growth forecast from 0.5% to 0.4%, while second-quarter growth was zero.
items.impact: Weak domestic demand and investment show that the growth engine has lost clear momentum.

items.development: Oil and gas price increases linked to the Iran war pushed the government into G7 discussions on energy intervention.
items.impact: Exposure to energy prices is pressuring consumption, industry and public finances at the same time.

items.development: Banque de France reports that international trade continues to support exports despite weak domestic demand.
items.impact: Exports are partly offsetting weakness in domestic demand.

items.development: The Osez l'IA programme reached more than 35,000 companies in one year and created 615 AI ambassadors.
items.impact: Spreading AI adoption across SMEs and companies could strengthen medium-term productivity capacity.

items.development: The central bank says corporate investment remains cautious because of high rates and uncertainty.
items.impact: Weak private-investment appetite limits future capacity and productivity growth.

items.development: The Finance Ministry expects public debt to reach 119.3% of GDP in 2026.
items.impact: Rising debt and interest costs narrow fiscal space for infrastructure and transformation spending.

items.development: Uncertainty continues over passing €54 billion of savings in the 2027 budget through a fragmented parliament.
items.impact: Political uncertainty around implementation speed could reduce economic-response capacity.

items.development: Unemployment rose 0.2 percentage points to 8.3% in the second quarter, one of the highest levels since 2019.
items.impact: Weaker labour demand shows the economic slowdown feeding into employment.

items.development: August inflation was 2.4%, while household confidence remained at 86 and purchasing power stayed under pressure.
items.impact: Pressure on real incomes weakens day-to-day household economics and consumer confidence.

items.development: Broad strikes took place in energy, transport and other sectors in September over the budget and cost of living.
items.impact: Intense social bargaining and parliamentary fragmentation reduce near-term policy predictability.

items.development: The economy grew 7.8% in April–June, while Moody's raised its FY2027 forecast to 7%.
items.impact: Investment- and manufacturing-led growth shows the economic engine remains strong.

items.development: The crude-oil import bill rose 25.8% year on year in August to $16.69 billion.
items.impact: High oil prices directly pressure the current account, the rupee and inflation.

items.development: Goods and services exports rose 25.4% year on year in August to $82.68 billion.
items.impact: Growth in electronics, engineering, automotive and services exports strengthens the external-demand base.

items.development: Wipro freed capacity equivalent to 20,000 employees through AI applications and trained more than 100,000 employees in advanced AI skills.
items.impact: Active AI adoption in the large IT sector strengthens technological adaptation of the current services model.

items.development: Strong investment and manufacturing activity were among the main drivers of 7.8% growth in the second quarter.
items.impact: Capital formation contributing to growth supports long-term capacity.

items.development: Moody's says rising defence and infrastructure spending could slow fiscal consolidation.
items.impact: Infrastructure spending supports growth, while energy and defence outlays can narrow budget room.

items.development: The RBI increased bond sales to absorb excess liquidity as markets priced in a possible rate increase.
items.impact: The policy response may support financial stability but tightens financing conditions.

items.development: August unemployment fell to a six-month low of 5%, while labour-force participation rose to 55.6%.
items.impact: Falling unemployment alongside higher participation is supportive for the labour market.

items.development: August inflation rose to 4.82%, the highest level in the new series.
items.impact: Energy and broader price increases create renewed pressure on real household incomes.

items.development: Higher US H-1B costs are leading major companies such as Alphabet to expand some operations in India.
items.impact: A shift of global technology work toward India could broaden local opportunities for highly skilled workers.

items.development: The BOT expects growth of 2.3% in 2026 and 1.8% in 2027, saying a return to potential could take several years.
items.impact: The economy is still growing, but structurally low speed remains a risk for the main growth engine.

items.development: Second-quarter growth was directly affected by high energy costs and travel disruptions linked to the Middle East.
items.impact: Dependence on energy imports and international tourism creates sensitivity to external geopolitical shocks.

items.development: July exports continued to grow, supported by the global electronics and AI cycle.
items.impact: Stronger technology exports provide external support against weak domestic demand.

items.development: Electric and hybrid vehicles reached 55% of the new-car market in the first seven months of the year.
items.impact: Thailand's ability to move its traditional automotive base into the EV era is strengthening materially.

items.development: The BOI's September agenda includes new high-tech investments and a $3.66 billion fast-tracked industrial project pipeline.
items.impact: Domestic and foreign capital moving into technology manufacturing is creating new growth engines.

items.development: Public spending by central government and state enterprises rose in July as the government accelerated industrial projects.
items.impact: Public support and infrastructure investment complement private-sector transformation.

items.development: The EV tax system was redesigned to directly encourage local content, investment and supplier development.
items.impact: Rapid regulatory adaptation to sector transformation supports competitiveness of the manufacturing base.

items.development: The BOT describes the labour market as broadly stable, while flagging manufacturing employment for close monitoring.
items.impact: Today's employment balance is stable, but the labour impact of manufacturing transformation is not yet clear.

items.development: The BOT says high household debt and rising living costs are weighing on domestic consumption.
items.impact: Highly indebted households' sensitivity to costs is a major vulnerability for living standards and domestic demand.

items.development: Thailand decided to reduce visa-free tourist stays for citizens of 93 countries from 60 to 30 days.
items.impact: The change reduces ease of longer stays under tourist status, while not directly altering other work and residence routes.

items.development: Industrial production grew 5.2% in August, while retail-sales growth was only 0.4%.
items.impact: Strong production alongside weak consumption keeps the domestic-demand imbalance in the economic model in place.

items.development: Weak consumption and property investment are making the economy more dependent on external demand and exports.
items.impact: If global trade tensions rise, domestic demand may have limited capacity to offset export losses.

items.development: Exports rose 18.6% year on year in August and total foreign trade grew 19.8%.
items.impact: Strong exports remain one of the most important buffers in the current growth model.

items.development: High-tech manufacturing grew 16.7%, battery output 57.2% and industrial-robot output 34.6%.
items.impact: Rapid expansion of next-generation industrial capacity strengthens China's position in technology competition.

items.development: Fixed-asset investment fell 7.2% in the first eight months, private investment 10.1% and property investment 19.9%.
items.impact: Broad weakness in private-capital appetite constrains future domestic growth capacity.

items.development: Infrastructure investment fell 4% year on year in the first eight months despite public support.
items.impact: The fact that state support has not yet fully reversed declines in private and infrastructure investment is an important early signal.

items.development: Regulators tightened IPO processes for humanoid-robot companies over valuation and commercialisation concerns.
items.impact: The intervention limits speculative capital and signals a more selective phase in financing strategic sectors.

items.development: Youth unemployment for non-students aged 16–24 reached a one-year high of 18.9% in August.
items.impact: Difficulties integrating young talent into the labour market pressure consumption and long-term human capital.

items.development: New-home prices fell 3% year on year in August while property investment declined 19.9%.
items.impact: Cheaper housing helps some buyers, but the property crisis still dominates wealth effects and consumer confidence.

items.development: Weak retail demand is being accompanied by youth unemployment of 18.9%.
items.impact: Persistent mismatch between young workers and economic opportunities could increase social and economic pressure.

items.development: IW raised its 2026 growth forecast from 0.4% to 1.2%, but expects momentum to slow in the second half.
items.impact: Public spending and exports are supporting a recovery, but durable private-sector growth has not yet emerged.

items.development: August inflation rose to 2.9%, influenced by energy prices.
items.impact: Renewed pressure from energy prices shows that Germany's core industrial vulnerability remains.

items.development: IW expects exports to grow 2.8% in 2026, while citing Chinese competition and protectionism as key risks.
items.impact: Exports are recovering, but the external-trade model faces a structurally harder global environment.

items.development: Volkswagen sharply cut its profit outlook as Chinese demand, Asian competitors and the EV transition accelerate restructuring.
items.impact: Transformation pressure in automotive continues to challenge Germany's most critical industrial ecosystem.

items.development: IW says private investment remains weak and high energy costs are weighing on investment appetite.
items.impact: The absence of a strong return in private capital delays formation of a new growth model.

items.development: A significant part of the upward revision to 2026 growth comes from higher public spending.
items.impact: Transmission of fiscal expansion into the economy increases the capacity to reduce years of underinvestment.

items.development: Industrial orders rose 2.5% in July, but fell 1.4% excluding large orders, while production declined 1.1%.
items.impact: New demand not translating broadly into production shows that adaptation is not yet complete.

items.development: Germany still has skilled-worker shortages in 157 occupations, while the share of foreign workers has doubled since 2014.
items.impact: Migration helps reduce labour shortages, but an ageing population is increasing structural reliance on external talent.

items.development: Energy-driven inflation rose to 2.9%, while housing costs remain a major economic issue, especially in large cities such as Berlin.
items.impact: Housing and energy costs are eroding the cost-of-living advantage in major cities.

items.development: September state elections showed votes shifting away from traditional centrist parties amid concerns over the economy, living costs and migration.
items.impact: Greater political fragmentation could make coalition-building and implementation of major economic reforms more complex.

items.development: August exports rose 68.7% year on year to $98.25 billion, driven mainly by semiconductors.
items.impact: AI-led chip demand is keeping the growth engine strong, while making the economy more dependent on the technology cycle.

items.development: Semiconductors accounted for roughly 41% of total exports in January–August.
items.impact: Concentration in one technology cycle increases vulnerability to a correction in global chip demand.

items.development: January–August exports rose 76% to China and 57% to the United States, with total exports already exceeding last year's full-year record.
items.impact: Strong demand in two major markets supports trade, but US–China tensions create a risk that could affect both at once.

items.development: The government accelerated a KRW 5 trillion semiconductor fund and water, power and R&D infrastructure plans for large chip clusters.
items.impact: Shifting capacity toward AI and advanced semiconductors helps carry the country's industrial advantage into the next technology cycle.

items.development: Talks are advancing on the first projects under South Korea's $350 billion US investment commitment.
items.impact: A broader global production footprint can improve market access, but outward capital allocation creates a balance to watch for domestic investment.

items.development: Chip clusters are planned to receive 650,000 tonnes of water per day by 2030 and 14.7 GW of power capacity by 2041.
items.impact: Scaling critical production infrastructure in advance reduces physical bottlenecks to industrial growth.

items.development: The government is preparing special-zone legislation to accelerate permits and infrastructure for chip clusters.
items.impact: Streamlining processes around strategic industry can speed the conversion of investment into execution.

items.development: Employment rose by 184,000 year on year in August, while conditions for young workers remained weak.
items.impact: Overall job growth adds resilience, but weak youth integration could constrain long-term talent supply.

items.development: Housing affordability and tight credit rules became major sources of public economic dissatisfaction in September.
items.impact: Difficult housing access, especially in Seoul, raises settlement costs and constrains household mobility.

items.development: Public pressure over housing and living costs increased, while no major new opening or restriction appeared for skilled international labour.
items.impact: Social pressure may shape economic policy, but there is no clear regime shift in talent openness for now.

items.development: Brazil's economy grew 0.5% quarter on quarter and 2.0% year on year in the second quarter, but slowed clearly from the first quarter.
items.impact: Continued growth is supportive, although high interest rates are reducing momentum in consumption and industry.

items.development: Mining exports rose 70.5% and crude-oil exports 126.2% year on year in the first two weeks of September.
items.impact: Strong commodity revenues support the external balance while keeping growth sensitive to commodity prices.

items.development: Exports rose 28.5% year on year in the first two weeks of September and the trade surplus reached $3.36 billion.
items.impact: Strong external demand provides an important buffer for a slowing domestic economy.

items.development: Industrial and services momentum weakened in the second quarter, while manufactured exports rose 17% in the first two weeks of September.
items.impact: Stronger manufactured exports are positive, but weak domestic industrial momentum limits transformation capacity.

items.development: High borrowing costs are weighing on companies and households, while economic activity fell 0.2% month on month in July.
items.impact: Persistently high capital costs make it harder for private investment to accelerate.

items.development: A wide fiscal deficit combined with high interest rates is keeping debt-servicing costs elevated.
items.impact: Limited fiscal space makes financing large infrastructure and transformation programmes more expensive.

items.development: After inflation eased to 4.22% in August, the central bank began gradually loosening tight monetary policy.
items.impact: A gradual balance between inflation control and growth supports near-term financial stability.

items.development: Unemployment fell to 5.4% in the second quarter, while the population reached 214.2 million.
items.impact: Low unemployment supports domestic demand and the tax base, though wage pressure may keep services inflation firm.

items.development: Household consumption fell 0.4% in the second quarter as high credit costs constrained spending.
items.impact: High borrowing costs pressure middle-class consumption and access to housing.

items.development: Fiscal and growth policies remain central to the public agenda ahead of the October elections, while no major monthly change occurred in the skilled foreign-worker regime.
items.impact: The election period raises short-term policy uncertainty, but there is no clear regime shift in talent access.

items.development: Official expectations point to growth of around 1% in 2026, with defence spending still providing major support.
items.impact: State spending preserves short-term activity, but stagnation in the civilian economy weakens the quality of growth.

items.development: The 2026 oil-production forecast was cut to a 17-year low of about 9.88 million barrels per day amid the effects of the war.
items.impact: Declining energy production weakens a key buffer for public revenues and the external balance.

items.development: EU bans and refinery disruptions are increasingly redirecting Russian energy flows toward markets such as China and India.
items.impact: A narrower set of markets reduces pricing power and external-trade flexibility.

items.development: Sanctions and restricted technology access are causing long-term erosion in civilian production capacity and technological competitiveness.
items.impact: Weaker access to critical technology and capital goods raises the cost of future industrial transformation.

items.development: High interest rates, war-related uncertainty and loss of confidence are weakening private-investment appetite.
items.impact: Capital concentrating in defence and state-linked sectors limits future capacity in the civilian economy.

items.development: The budget deficit has risen to roughly 2.8% of GDP, while reserve funds and high military spending narrow fiscal room.
items.impact: Rising war costs squeeze resources available for infrastructure and civilian public spending.

items.development: After refinery attacks and fuel shortages, the government imposed temporary restrictions on exports of gasoline, diesel and jet fuel.
items.impact: Rapid supply management can protect the domestic market in the short term, but does not repair structural damage to production capacity.

items.development: Unemployment remains around 2%, while companies struggle to find skilled labour because of war, migration and demographic contraction.
items.impact: Very low unemployment signals labour scarcity rather than healthy slack, constraining production capacity.

items.development: Inflation remains above 6%, while fuel and basic consumer costs and high credit rates weigh on household spending.
items.impact: Pressure on real living costs weakens consumption and settlement appeal.

items.development: War-driven migration, sanctions and economic isolation continue to restrict international talent and capital mobility.
items.impact: A smaller talent pool and weaker international links reduce long-term innovation capacity.

items.development: The IMF expects 4.6% growth in fiscal year 2026 and sees the impact of the regional war becoming more visible in 2026–27.
items.impact: The economy remains resilient in the short term, but regional shocks could slow the new growth phase.

items.development: Middle East conflicts are affecting energy costs, tourism, logistics and external financing at the same time.
items.impact: Geopolitical risk hitting several income and cost channels keeps Egypt highly exposed to external shocks.

items.development: Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd decided in September to return four additional container services to the Suez Canal.
items.impact: A gradual return of canal traffic is a positive normalisation signal for foreign-currency revenues and logistics activity.

items.development: The government said it is continuing a programme of state-company stake sales and a larger private-sector role in the economy.
items.impact: Reducing the state's weight could create more room for private investment and competition, but execution speed will be decisive.

items.development: The IMF expects the regional war to result in weaker investment and higher financing costs in 2026–27.
items.impact: Slower private-capital investment could make it harder to turn growth into a durable cycle.

items.development: Completion of the IMF's seventh review opened access to about $1.8 billion of new financing.
items.impact: External financing and fiscal discipline provide a short-term buffer, while debt and subsidy-reform pressures remain.

items.development: The IMF cited exchange-rate flexibility, fuel-price adjustments and spending control among rapid policy responses to the regional shock.
items.impact: Fast policy response supports macro stability, but the social cost and durability of reforms need monitoring.

items.development: Population growth remains strong, while creating enough productive jobs for a young workforce is still a core structural challenge.
items.impact: A large labour pool is a potential advantage, but job creation remains critical for inclusive growth.

items.development: Annual urban inflation was 14.5% in August, while housing, water, electricity, gas and fuel rose 33% year on year.
items.impact: High basic living costs are putting strong pressure on household budgets and real purchasing power.

items.development: Tourism expectations of roughly 20.2 million visitors and higher revenues in 2026 point to continued strong international access.
items.impact: Openness in tourism and services supports jobs and foreign-currency earnings, while no major monthly change appeared in skilled-talent policy.

items.development: Second-quarter GDP grew 0.2% quarter on quarter, and ISTAT expects 2026 growth of around 0.8%.
items.impact: Growth is positive but slow, leaving a limited buffer against external shocks.

items.development: August inflation rose to 3.3% year on year, driven by a strong increase in energy prices.
items.impact: Energy becoming a major driver again raises vulnerability to external shocks for industry and households.

items.development: With global supply-chain uncertainty continuing, second-quarter growth was supported more by consumption and investment.
items.impact: A growth mix less dependent on external demand provides a near-term buffer, though global risks remain for export-oriented industry.

items.development: Industrial production rose 0.7% month on month in July after two months of decline, with recovery across major non-energy groups.
items.impact: A return to industrial growth is positive for transformation capacity, but one month does not confirm a lasting trend.

items.development: Private investment made a positive contribution to second-quarter growth.
items.impact: Investment supporting growth is a constructive signal for production capacity.

items.development: Public debt is expected to rise to about 139% of GDP in 2026 as debt-servicing costs increase quickly.
items.impact: High debt and interest costs narrow fiscal room for infrastructure and transformation investment.

items.development: The government emphasises long-term political stability, while progress on public administration, health and education reforms remains contested.
items.impact: Political continuity supports decision-making, but the pace of structural-reform implementation remains a key watchpoint.

items.development: July unemployment fell to 5.8%, while much of employment growth is concentrated among people aged 50–64.
items.impact: Low unemployment is positive, but an ageing workforce limits long-term demographic capacity.

items.development: Consumer inflation rose to 3.3% in August, with energy the main driver.
items.impact: Energy-led price pressure hurts real household incomes and living costs.

items.development: Debate over migration and integration intensified again in September around education and border policy.
items.impact: Discussion of a tighter migration regime may reduce policy predictability for foreign workers, although final rules are not yet settled.

items.development: Monthly economic activity in June rose 0.8% year on year, while the 2027 budget assumes roughly 3% growth for 2026.
items.impact: The economy has returned to growth, but industry and labour data show the recovery remains uneven.

items.development: Energy and agricultural exports remain critical to the external balance, while a $51 billion project to turn Vaca Muerta into an LNG export hub applied under RIGI.
items.impact: More energy-export capacity could reduce foreign-currency dependence, although execution risk on the mega-project remains high.

items.development: Exports were $8.88 billion and imports $6.70 billion in August, producing a trade surplus for the 33rd consecutive month.
items.impact: Persistent trade surpluses support reserve accumulation and currency stability.

items.development: Manufacturing output fell 5% year on year in July, while LNG and energy infrastructure are emerging as a new growth axis.
items.impact: New energy capacity creates opportunity, but manufacturing contraction raises the transition cost between sectors.

items.development: The $51 billion Argentina LNG project's application to the RIGI investment regime strengthened the goal of attracting large-scale foreign capital.
items.impact: If realised, the project could materially increase capital inflows and export capacity, but the full investment is not yet secured.

items.development: The 2027 draft budget keeps a fiscal-discipline stance and assumes roughly 29% inflation and 3% growth for 2026.
items.impact: A balanced-budget focus may support stability, but keeps room for infrastructure and social spending limited.

items.development: The central bank continued reserve purchases but slowed the pace in September to preserve market balance.
items.impact: More flexible reserve management supports currency stability while leaving more room for private FX demand.

items.development: Second-quarter unemployment was 7.9% and labour-force participation 48.9%.
items.impact: Labour-market slack pressures household incomes while keeping labour supply relatively broad for employers.

items.development: Monthly consumer inflation slowed to 1.7% in August, but annual price levels and income adjustment remain major household pressures.
items.impact: Slower monthly inflation is an improvement in living-cost dynamics, although purchasing power has not fully normalised.

items.development: Continuation of economic reforms and the 2027 election calendar are making policy continuity an important factor in investment and migration decisions.
items.impact: Uncertainty over reform durability may create a short-term wait-and-see stance among international talent and capital.

items.development: Second-quarter GDP grew 0.8% quarter on quarter and 2.5% year on year.
items.impact: Growth remaining above the euro-area average points to a strong economic engine.

items.development: August inflation rose to 3.3%, while energy prices increased 12.2% year on year.
items.impact: Sensitivity to energy prices remains an important external-shock channel for households and small businesses.

items.development: Net external demand turned positive in the second quarter as exports grew faster than imports.
items.impact: Strong exports and services demand provide an important buffer against slower domestic demand.

items.development: Services turnover rose 2.1% year on year in July, while new housing permits and completed homes increased.
items.impact: Growth in services and emerging housing supply support two important structural needs at once.

items.development: The contribution of domestic demand to growth fell markedly in the second quarter as investment slowed.
items.impact: Weaker investment momentum raises the question of whether private capital can take over from EU funds as a growth driver.

items.development: The government is running an EU-backed programme of about €9 billion to deliver 150,000 affordable homes by 2030.
items.impact: The large housing programme could reduce the supply gap, but labour and execution capacity will determine speed.

items.development: Licensing is being simplified to accelerate housing production, while construction faces an estimated labour shortage of 80,000–120,000 people.
items.impact: Even with simpler regulation, human-capital shortages may limit actual delivery speed.

items.development: Unemployment stayed at 5.7% in June, while tighter migration rules are reported to be widening labour shortages in sectors such as construction.
items.impact: Low unemployment is positive, but lower migration creates capacity bottlenecks in fast-growing sectors.

items.development: Portugal's housing shortage is estimated at around 300,000 units, while new rents in Lisbon place a very high burden on average incomes.
items.impact: The housing supply gap remains the country's clearest cost and accessibility risk for relocation.

items.development: Tighter migration rules are reducing net migration while staffing shortages grow in sectors reliant on foreign workers.
items.impact: A stricter migration regime reduces international talent access and capacity in sectors such as construction.

items.development: The Dutch economy grew 0.4% quarter on quarter and 1.3% year on year in the second quarter, with consumption making the largest contribution.
items.impact: Moderate but balanced growth supports economic resilience.

items.development: August inflation rose to 3.3%, while global energy and transport costs remain risks to the price outlook.
items.impact: External energy and trade shocks can pass quickly into household and company costs in the open economy.

items.development: Exports rose 1.2% in the second quarter and imports 1.4%, making net trade contribution slightly negative.
items.impact: Exports are still growing, but faster import growth limits trade's contribution to expansion.

items.development: Manufacturing output rose 4.6% year on year in June, while machinery and electronics exports grew.
items.impact: Strength in high-value manufacturing and electronics supports technological transformation capacity.

items.development: Fixed-asset investment rose 2.7% year on year in June, while total investment increased 0.5% quarter on quarter in Q2.
items.impact: Positive investment shows companies still have confidence in future capacity.

items.development: Public consumption rose 0.4% in the second quarter, with healthcare and public-sector wage spending supporting growth.
items.impact: Public spending supports activity, but resolving housing and grid bottlenecks still depends on infrastructure investment speed.

items.development: Although 9 of 13 CBS business-cycle indicators remained below their long-term trend, the overall picture improved in August from July.
items.impact: Even without broad acceleration, the halt in deterioration gives policymakers and companies more time to adapt.

items.development: August unemployment remained at 4.0%, while the number of unemployed rose by an average 3,000 per month over the last three months.
items.impact: The labour market remains tight, but gradual cooling could ease talent shortages somewhat.

items.development: Existing-home prices rose 3.9% year on year in July and supply pressure in the housing market persists.
items.impact: Slower price growth is positive, but high housing costs remain a major relocation barrier.

items.development: Immigration was 23,148 in July and emigration 24,524, turning monthly net migration slightly negative.
items.impact: Weaker net migration could limit population and labour-force growth, but one month does not indicate a lasting regime change.

items.development: Romania's economy was flat quarter on quarter in Q2 2026, contracted 0.4% year on year and GDP fell 0.8% in the first half.
items.impact: Weak growth and pressure on domestic demand limit near-term economic resilience.

items.development: Pipeline construction started for the Neptun Deep Black Sea gas project, and national gas output is expected to roughly double when production begins in 2027.
items.impact: More domestic gas capacity could reduce dependence on energy imports and exposure to external supply shocks.

items.development: Exports rose 3.1% and imports 2.0% in January–July, while the trade deficit narrowed 1.1% year on year to €19.28 billion.
items.impact: Faster export growth is positive, but the large trade deficit continues to pressure the external balance.

items.development: Dacia and Ford temporarily halted production in August because of power-supply problems, exposing energy-infrastructure risk in export-oriented automotive manufacturing.
items.impact: Faster industrial transformation requires production capacity to be strengthened alongside the power grid and supply security.

items.development: FDI into Romania fell to €1.13 billion in January–July 2026 from €4.92 billion in the same period of 2025.
items.impact: The sharp drop in capital inflows is a weak signal for new capacity investment and growth financing.

items.development: The European Commission expects a 2026 budget deficit of 6.2% of GDP while public investment rises to around 7% of GDP.
items.impact: High public investment supports infrastructure, while the large deficit limits fiscal room.

items.development: The European Commission said effective steps were taken in June on excessive-deficit correction, while strengthening public administration and investment-delivery capacity remained priorities.
items.impact: The reform direction is positive, but structural execution gaps could slow transformation.

items.development: Eurostat put July unemployment at 6.4%, while the latest youth-unemployment rate remained 30.8% in June.
items.impact: Persistently high youth unemployment pressures labour matching and the long-term talent pool.

items.development: Romania's annual inflation was 6.3% in August, the highest in the European Union.
items.impact: High price growth raises household costs and day-to-day living expenses for people considering relocation.

items.development: Romania launched the WorkinRomania platform in August to digitise foreign-worker hiring and introduced the D/AM1 route for highly skilled workers.
items.impact: More digital and centralised processes can improve international talent access and help close labour shortages.

items.development: Canada's economy grew 0.8% in real terms in Q2 2026, driven by exports, household spending and business investment.
items.impact: Renewed acceleration in growth supports economic resilience.

items.development: Goods exports to the United States fell 6.6% in July, but the US still accounted for roughly two-thirds of total goods exports at about C$50.5 billion.
items.impact: High dependence on the US market means trade tensions can quickly affect Canadian growth and industry.

items.development: Goods exports fell 2.3% in July while imports rose 2.2%, shrinking the goods-trade surplus from C$4.2 billion to C$769 million; non-US exports hit a record C$25.6 billion.
items.impact: Trade momentum weakened overall, but progress in market diversification partly offsets US-related risk.

items.development: Bell's AI infrastructure investment in Saskatchewan is being expanded toward 1.2 GW of capacity and as much as C$52.5 billion in total capital investment.
items.impact: Large-scale AI and data-centre investment is building new strategic capacity across energy, compute and digital infrastructure.

source.name: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada

items.development: FDI into Canada rose from C$18.8 billion to C$25.9 billion in the second quarter, with more than half going to manufacturing and finance/insurance.
items.impact: Higher direct investment strengthens the capital base for new capacity and productivity investment.

items.development: The Build Communities Strong Fund provides C$51 billion of new public infrastructure investment over 10 years beginning in 2026–27.
items.impact: Long-term infrastructure financing can expand housing, transport and essential-service capacity.

items.development: Fifteen projects announced under the Major Projects Office represent more than C$125 billion in capital investment, with faster federal reviews targeted.
items.impact: Centralising project approvals could speed execution, but durable impact depends on actual delivery performance.

items.development: Employment fell 0.2% month on month in August while unemployment remained at 6.4%.
items.impact: Weaker employment shows the labour market's ability to support growth remains limited.

items.development: Annual inflation was 3.0% in August, rents rose 2.8% nationwide, and grocery prices remained 29% above 2021 levels.
items.impact: Price and rent pressure keep household budgets and the total cost of relocating to Canada high.

items.development: The 2026–2028 immigration plan keeps the permanent-resident target at 380,000 a year, cuts the 2026 temporary-resident intake target to 385,000 and raises the economic-immigration share.
items.impact: Canada continues to attract skilled talent while moving toward tighter capacity management in student and temporary-worker channels.

potential_countries.name: Poland
potential_countries.selection_reason: Growth, EU funding and accelerating domestic defence production are creating new capacity at the same time.

items.development: Poland's GDP grew 3.9% year on year in the second quarter of 2026.
items.impact: Strong domestic momentum despite weakness around the euro area makes Poland worth watching for near-term growth.

items.development: August inflation rose to 3.4%, transport prices increased 3.5% month on month and the government planned a new windfall tax on oil companies.
items.impact: Global energy shocks still pass quickly into households and fiscal policy, keeping energy costs a core vulnerability.

items.development: More than 50 agreements worth over €1 billion were signed under the Carpathian Eight initiative for regional trade, energy and logistics.
items.impact: New regional links could strengthen Poland's role in Central and Eastern European trade corridors.

items.development: Domestic and Central European defence procurement has roughly quadrupled since 2022 to PLN 30.4 billion.
items.impact: Directing defence spending toward local production is building technology transfer, manufacturing capacity and regional supply chains.

items.development: Poland received roughly PLN 31 billion of new EU funding in June under its National Recovery Plan.
items.impact: EU capital directed to energy, digitalisation, health and defence supports the investment cycle.

items.development: New EU funds are being allocated to energy infrastructure, clean transport, water management and digital-transformation projects.
items.impact: Large-scale external funding expands fiscal capacity for infrastructure modernisation.

items.development: A planned windfall tax to soften fuel prices had previously faced a presidential veto and the legal process continues.
items.impact: Economic intervention capacity is strong, but friction between institutions can slow execution.

items.development: The population fell by 159,000 year on year in the first half of 2026, while net international migration remained positive; Q2 LFS unemployment was 3.2%.
items.impact: Very low unemployment is an advantage, while natural population decline pressures long-term labour supply.

items.development: Real corporate wages rose 3.6% year on year in July, while completed housing units increased 3.2% in January–July.
items.impact: Real wage growth and new housing supply partly offset cost-of-living pressure.

items.development: Despite population decline, net international migration remained positive in the first half of 2026.
items.impact: Migration partly offsets labour shortages, creating both a structural need and opportunity for international talent.

potential_countries.name: Vietnam
potential_countries.selection_reason: Industrial production, FDI, exports and capital-market access are accelerating at the same time.

items.development: Industrial production rose 14.4% year on year in August and 11.9% in the first eight months.
items.impact: Broad-based production momentum shows the economic engine is running strongly.

items.development: FDI companies accounted for 80.1% of exports in the first eight months, while the US was the largest export market and China the largest import market.
items.impact: Concentration on foreign capital and two major external markets creates sensitivity to trade shocks.

items.development: Total goods trade rose 28.7% year on year in the first eight months to $770.14 billion, with exports up 22.4%.
items.impact: Rapid expansion in global supply chains strengthens the external-demand engine.

items.development: Manufactured products accounted for 90.2% of exports in the first eight months while industrial output grew at double-digit rates.
items.impact: The shift toward higher-value manufacturing is expanding strategic-sector capacity.

items.development: Registered foreign investment rose 55.4% in the first eight months to $40.63 billion, while realised FDI reached $17.25 billion.
items.impact: Strong capital inflows are a leading indicator of new production and service capacity.

items.development: State-budget investment spending rose 18.5% year on year in the first eight months.
items.impact: Faster public investment can reduce bottlenecks in logistics and production infrastructure.

items.development: Vietnam entered the FTSE Russell emerging-market index, while reforms such as a central-counterparty clearing system continue for MSCI access.
items.impact: Concrete capital-market reform results strengthen execution capacity, while remaining access constraints still need monitoring.

items.development: Employment in industrial companies rose 3.8% year on year as of 1 August.
items.impact: Industrial growth translating into jobs signals strong labour demand.

items.development: August CPI rose 4.89% year on year, while 96.5% of households said income was unchanged or higher than a year earlier.
items.impact: The income outlook remains resilient, but faster inflation creates new cost-of-living pressure.

items.development: US and Vietnamese companies are preparing a broad new package of agreements across energy, technology, aviation and finance.
items.impact: Deeper integration with international companies is a positive talent signal for skilled jobs and technology transfer.

potential_countries.name: Indonesia
potential_countries.selection_reason: The large domestic market and nickel-battery industrial policy are strong, but fiscal and institutional-trust signals need close monitoring.

items.development: Bank Indonesia says domestic demand and fiscal stimulus are supporting growth, with July real retail sales expected to rise 0.9% year on year.
items.impact: The large domestic market provides a buffer against external shocks, although consumption momentum is not yet very strong.

items.development: High global oil prices are raising fuel-subsidy costs while the rupiah remains under pressure from global volatility.
items.impact: Energy imports and currency sensitivity are critical external dependencies for the fiscal balance and inflation.

items.development: The trade balance recorded a $3.58 billion surplus in January–June, while June alone posted a $0.45 billion deficit.
items.impact: The external balance is broadly supportive, but monthly volatility shows dependence on commodities and global demand.

items.development: A new nickel-pricing formula makes lower-grade ore more economical for HPAL battery producers.
items.impact: The regulation supports Indonesia's shift from raw-material exports into the EV-battery value chain.

items.development: Portfolio investment recorded a net inflow of $1.8 billion in Q3 2026 through 14 August.
items.impact: Continued foreign-capital inflows support growth and currency stability, while policy confidence remains critical.

items.development: The new finance minister said the 2026 budget deficit would be kept at 2.85% of GDP, below the legal 3% ceiling.
items.impact: The fiscal-discipline commitment supports financial resilience despite large social and infrastructure programmes.

items.development: After the third finance minister change in less than two years, the new leadership pledged policy continuity and predictability.
items.impact: Technocratic continuity may restore confidence, but frequent senior changes keep institutional-predictability risk alive.

items.development: The labour force reached 155.41 million in May 2026 while unemployment fell to 4.65%.
items.impact: A large and growing labour force is a major structural advantage for scaling manufacturing and services.

items.development: The share of households with access to adequate housing rose from 68.4% to 70.3% in 2026, while August inflation was 3.19%.
items.impact: Better housing access supports relocation conditions, although regional cost differences remain important.

items.development: High-skill industrial investment is rising while labour-force participation increased to 70.57%.
items.impact: A broad labour base and new industrial projects are expanding the talent market, though governance confidence still matters for foreign professionals.

potential_countries.name: Saudi Arabia
potential_countries.selection_reason: The non-oil economy and Vision 2030 capital transition are strong, while energy and regional-security vulnerabilities are being stress-tested.

items.development: The IMF expects 2.6% non-oil growth in 2026, while S&P says non-oil activity has reached roughly 70% of GDP.
items.impact: A larger non-oil base shows economic diversification becoming more tangible.

items.development: Houthi attacks disabled the East-West oil pipeline, showing that the alternative export route is also vulnerable.
items.impact: Exposure of oil and logistics infrastructure to regional-security shocks remains the country's most critical dependency.

items.development: Saudi oil shipments began to recover in September using alternative transfer methods and routes through Hormuz.
items.impact: The ability to maintain exports through alternative logistics improves resilience of external revenues.

items.development: PIF created a new company to develop tourism and housing on the Al-Khafji coast, while investment continues to shift toward non-oil sectors.
items.impact: Capital moving into tourism, housing and services strengthens the sector-diversification axis of Vision 2030.

items.development: S&P views more selective calibration of Vision 2030 investment and a larger private-sector role positively for fiscal resilience.
items.impact: More selective and private-sector-led capital allocation could improve investment efficiency.

items.development: S&P maintained the A+ rating and highlighted strong public assets and calibrated spending as fiscal buffers.
items.impact: Large public assets provide significant financial capacity to continue major transformation projects.

items.development: The IMF cited rerouted logistics and reprioritised project spending as signs of economic agility despite the war shock.
items.impact: Fast operational response capacity appears strong, although the security environment raises execution costs.

items.development: The IMF says Saudi unemployment remains low and highlights progress in female labour-force participation as a Vision 2030 gain.
items.impact: A more diverse labour base strengthens local talent capacity in non-oil sectors.

items.development: August inflation remained at 1.8%, while housing, water and energy rose 3.9% year on year.
items.impact: Overall inflation is low, but housing costs increase relocation costs, especially in fast-growing cities.

items.development: A new collective-housing regulation brought 1,360 licensed facilities serving roughly one million foreign workers under formal standards.
items.impact: Institutionalising foreign-worker living conditions is a positive signal for international-labour infrastructure.

potential_countries.name: Malaysia
potential_countries.selection_reason: High growth, semiconductor/AI infrastructure and strong foreign-investment inflows are scaling at the same time.

items.development: Malaysia's economy grew 6.0% year on year in Q2 2026, with manufacturing up 7.5% and services also strong.
items.impact: Expansion across both services and production shows a strong economic engine.

items.development: High oil prices are pressuring the ringgit, while the electronics trade surplus partly offsets higher energy-import costs.
items.impact: Energy prices and the dollar cycle are key external vulnerabilities, while strong electronics exports provide an important buffer.

items.development: June exports rose 45.4% year on year, led by electronics and AI-linked products.
items.impact: The surge in technology exports is making Malaysia more important in the AI-hardware supply chain.

items.development: Nvidia-backed Firmus signed a multi-year agreement to provide OpenAI with compute capacity from two Malaysian data centres.
items.impact: Scaling the AI data-centre ecosystem with real customer demand strengthens strategic technology transformation.

items.development: Approved investment in the first half rose 11.7% to MYR 218.5 billion, while foreign investment grew 18.5%.
items.impact: High and diversified capital inflows are a strong leading signal for future capacity and employment.

items.development: First-half investment projects are expected to create more than 99,000 jobs, with Johor and Selangor emerging as major investment hubs.
items.impact: Rapid growth of investment clusters creates opportunity while making energy and grid planning critical for urban capacity.

items.development: MIDA is repositioning data-centre policy from attracting investment toward generating more value for local SMEs and supply chains.
items.impact: Moving policy into a second phase shows adaptation capacity and aims to spread investment benefits through the local economy.

items.development: Employment rose 1.1% year on year in Q2, unemployment stayed at 3.0%, and labour productivity per hour increased 5.5%.
items.impact: Low unemployment and rising productivity support new high-value investment.

items.development: Unemployment remains at 3.0% and inflation relatively contained, but fast data-centre and investment growth may add housing and infrastructure pressure in hubs such as Johor.
items.impact: The overall household picture is balanced, but living-cost and capacity pressure in investment clusters needs close monitoring.

items.development: First-half approved projects are expected to create around 99,000 jobs, many in high-skill manufacturing and services.
items.impact: New technology investment is expanding the opportunity pool for local and international talent.
